splits.why: Planned page spans a whole book (Bridson-Haefliger alone has 24 chapters) and Wikipedia's GGT article lists over 20 separate themes. Keep the id as a short overview hub, or retire it.

math.GR and math.AT need cohomology of discrete groups (resolutions, K(G,1), Bass-Serre). Number theory needs profinite and Galois cohomology. Keep 'galois-cohomology' for the latter and depend on the new 'group-cohomology'.
Entropy theory (Kolmogorov-Sinai, variational principle) is a separate course-week, and thermodynamic formalism and Lyapunov exponents build on it.
Gilbarg-Trudinger gives maximum principles, Schauder theory and De Giorgi-Nash-Moser separate chapters. Narrow 'elliptic-pde' to L2 weak-solution theory and regularity (Evans ch. 6).
Keep Ext/Tor and derived functors on modules there. Abelian categories and triangulated or derived categories each fill a full chapter.
One page cannot hold Marker ch. 2-9; keep model-theory for structures, elementary maps, Löwenheim-Skolem and ultraproducts, and move QE, types/saturation and stability to their own pages.
math.OA papers assume each as a separate graduate course (Brown-Ozawa ch. 1 alone is a chapter); the existing page can become a short overview or be retired.
Keep forcing for the basics through the independence of CH (Jech ch. 14-15); iterated forcing, MA and proper forcing are Jech ch. 16 and 31 and appear in most current set-theory papers.
The research-stage page mixes the adelic representation-theory background (Bump ch. 3-4), which is tier 1 for math.NT, with the Langlands-programme overview; keep automorphic-forms as the overview.
Planned page should cover symplectic linear algebra, Darboux, Moser and Lagrangian neighbourhoods (Cannas da Silva Parts I-III); moment maps and reduction (Parts VIII-X) need their own page.
